policy.purpose: Evidence ledger for canonical Pattern Dictionary Wave 5 before runtime publication.
policy.runtime_lock: data/patterns.json remains canonical 80 throughout this source-verification gate.
policy.primary_palette_rule: A fixed primary palette is an editorial recognition reference unless a source establishes color as identity-relevant. It is never presented as the only valid colorway.
policy.relationship_rule: similar and often_confused_with are visual-discovery relationships, not claims of shared historical origin unless explicitly sourced.
policy.qualification_rule: Use qualified when the term is fundamentally a technique, textile tradition, textile style, or material-inspired visual family that does not resolve to one uniquely fixed motif.

patterns.term_scope: Central Asian embroidered textile tradition with many regional compositions rather than one fixed repeat
patterns.structure: Large embroidered rosettes, palmettes, flowers, stems and scrolling foliage are arranged across joined cotton or silk panels; composition varies by region and workshop.

color_guidance.reason: Floral embroidery structure is the recognition cue; palettes vary.

patterns.qualification: Suzani is a Central Asian embroidered textile tradition, not one universal repeat. The reference image is a representative recognition aid.

supports: suzani terminology and Central Asian textile context

patterns.term_scope: Ghanaian strip-woven textile tradition with many named arrangements rather than one fixed motif
patterns.structure: Narrow woven strips with colored warp/weft patterning are sewn edge-to-edge into larger cloths; blocks and bands of geometric color vary among designs.

color_guidance.reason: Bright sectional strip-weave patterning is a common recognition cue, but no single palette defines kente.

patterns.qualification: Kente is a Ghanaian strip-woven textile tradition with many designs and meanings, not one canonical repeat.

patterns.term_scope: Malian bogolanfini mud-dyed textile tradition with varied symbolic pattern vocabularies
patterns.structure: High-contrast dark and light fields use repeated lines, dots, chevrons and symbolic geometric units produced in a mud-dye textile tradition; exact layouts vary.

color_guidance.reason: Dark mud-dyed marks against pale cloth are a strong recognition cue; exact motifs vary.

patterns.qualification: Bogolan/bogolanfini is a mud-dyed Malian textile tradition with many encoded or named pattern arrangements, not one fixed motif.

sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of African Art

patterns.term_scope: Yoruba indigo resist-dyed textile tradition using multiple resist methods and named patterns
patterns.structure: Indigo fields are patterned by tied, stitched, folded, stencilled, or starch-resist methods, yielding white-to-blue dots, lines, grids, circles and named compositions.

color_guidance.reason: Indigo-and-resist contrast is historically central to recognition, while exact designs vary.

patterns.qualification: Adire is a Yoruba indigo resist-dyed textile tradition encompassing multiple methods and many named patterns, not one universal repeat.

supports: multiple resist methods including tying, stitching, folding, starch and stencil

patterns.term_scope: Kuba textile tradition using raffia and varied geometric embroidery/applique rather than one fixed motif
patterns.structure: Raffia panels carry angular, interlocking, interrupted, asymmetric geometric motifs made with embroidery, cut pile, applique, dyeing, or combinations.

color_guidance.reason: Raffia-toned ground and bold geometric interventions are common recognition cues, not a fixed palette.

patterns.qualification: Kuba cloth denotes a broad Central African raffia textile tradition with many techniques and patterns, not one universal repeat.

patterns.term_scope: Japanese running-stitch reinforcement and embroidery tradition with many geometric motifs
patterns.structure: Repeated running stitches form dotted white lines on cloth, often organized into grids, waves, diamonds, hemp-leaf-like geometry, or other named Japanese motifs.

color_guidance.reason: White running stitches on indigo are a strong traditional recognition cue, but sashiko exists in other colors.

patterns.qualification: Sashiko is a Japanese stitching and reinforcement tradition with many patterns, not one fixed motif.

supports: sashiko as traditional Japanese folk embroidery

patterns.term_scope: Bengal/Bangladesh layered-cloth running-stitch embroidery and quilting tradition with varied personal designs
patterns.structure: Layers of reused cloth are quilted with dense running stitches; embroidered figures, flowers, borders, spirals, and geometric fields may be added in highly varied compositions.

color_guidance.reason: Running-stitch texture is important; color and motif layouts are highly variable.

patterns.qualification: Kantha is a Bengal/Bangladesh quilting and embroidery tradition with diverse individual compositions, not one fixed repeat.

supports: layers of old garments quilted with running stitch

patterns.term_scope: Otomí/Tenango embroidery tradition with varied densely filled animal and plant figures
patterns.structure: Bright outlined animal, bird, plant and floral silhouettes are densely filled with embroidery and arranged as lively all-over scenes on plain cloth.

color_guidance.reason: Multicolor filled silhouettes are a common recognition cue, while palettes vary.

patterns.qualification: Otomi/Tenango embroidery is a living textile tradition with diverse compositions, not one fixed repeat.

sources.publisher: National Museum of the American Indian, Smithsonian
Museo Nacional de Culturas Populares / Google Arts & Culture

patterns.term_scope: Commercial wax-print textile style with many polychromatic motifs and complex transnational history

verified_names.ja: アフリカンワックスプリント

patterns.structure: Strong flat colors, outlined motifs, and repeating geometric, floral, figurative or symbolic units appear on printed cotton; motif vocabularies are extremely diverse.

color_guidance.reason: High-saturation flat multicolor printing is a common visual cue but no palette is definitional.

patterns.qualification: African wax print/Ankara names a broad printed-textile style and trade history with many motifs, not one fixed pattern.

supports: many layered polychromatic patterns and complex history

patterns.term_scope: Relief block-printing technique capable of many textile motifs rather than one fixed visual pattern
patterns.structure: Repeated impressions from carved blocks create visible modular repeats; slight registration variation and block boundaries may remain, across floral, geometric and figurative designs.

color_guidance.reason: Palette varies by workshop and dye process; repeated block impressions are the recognition cue.

patterns.qualification: Block print is a printing technique with many motif traditions, not one canonical motif.

supports: many designs and repeated block footprints

patterns.term_scope: named animal print imitating zebra striping
patterns.structure: Irregular high-contrast stripes run across the field, changing width and direction and often tapering or branching rather than forming uniform parallel bands.

color_guidance.reason: Black-and-white irregular striping is identity-relevant to the common zebra-print visual.

supports: stripes described as noncontinuous, unpredictable and changing direction

patterns.term_scope: named animal print imitating tiger coat stripes
patterns.structure: Dark narrow-to-medium stripes curve and taper across a warm orange/tan field, frequently with lighter or white areas.

color_guidance.reason: Orange/tan ground with dark tapered stripes is identity-relevant to conventional tiger print.

supports: white areas and individual stripe patterns

patterns.term_scope: named animal print imitating patterned snake scales or skin
patterns.structure: Small connected scale cells form a dense network, often with darker borders, mottled centers, or larger longitudinal patches layered over the scale texture.

color_guidance.reason: Scale-cell texture is identity-relevant; natural and fashion colorways vary widely.

supports: imitation snake-skin use in fashion accessories

patterns.term_scope: named animal print imitating piebald cattle markings
patterns.structure: Large irregular solid patches are scattered across a contrasting field, with soft organic edges and substantial open background between patches.

color_guidance.reason: Black-and-white piebald patches are identity-relevant to the common Holstein-inspired cow print.

supports: Holsteins recognized by distinctive black-and-white or red-and-white markings

patterns.term_scope: named animal print imitating giraffe coat patches
patterns.structure: Large tan-to-brown polygonal patches are separated by a lighter network of narrow channels, creating a cellular mosaic.

color_guidance.reason: Brown polygonal patches separated by pale channels are identity-relevant to the conventional giraffe-print visual.

supports: individual giraffes identified by unique spot patterns
giraffe coat spot pattern as recognition feature

patterns.term_scope: named animal print imitating Dalmatian dog spotting

ja: ダルメシアンスポット

patterns.structure: Numerous small-to-medium dark rounded or irregular spots are scattered individually across a light ground, with more open spacing than dense polka dots.

color_guidance.reason: Black/liver isolated spots on white are identity-relevant to the Dalmatian coat cue.

supports: spot size and distribution compared with patches

patterns.term_scope: camouflage visual family based on disruptive irregular patches rather than one single standardized repeat
patterns.structure: Overlapping irregular organic patches in several tones break up continuous contours; woodland-like versions often use greens, browns, tan and black.

color_guidance.reason: Earth-tone irregular disruptive patches are a common recognition cue, while camouflage systems vary.

sources.publisher: Smithsonian National Museum of American History

patterns.term_scope: resist-dye technique family created by binding cloth before dyeing rather than one fixed motif
patterns.structure: Bound or pinched areas resist dye, creating radiating rings, bursts, bands, diamonds, or irregular color transitions with soft feathered edges.

color_guidance.reason: Multicolor radiating effects are a common editorial cue, but tie-dye can be monochrome or many palettes.

patterns.qualification: Tie-dye is a resist-dye technique family; rings, spirals, diamonds and other effects depend on how cloth is bound and dyed.

supports: tie-dyed fabrics made by pinching and binding before dyeing
diamond design as one tie-dye outcome

patterns.term_scope: marbling technique and visual family made by floating color on a bath and transferring flowing patterns
patterns.structure: Flowing veins, swirls and feathered bands intermix without a fixed repeat; combing or stylus movement can organize the floating colors before transfer.

color_guidance.reason: Flowing multicolor veins are an editorial recognition cue; marbling palettes and tools vary.

patterns.qualification: Marbling is a technique and visual family, not one fixed motif. The reference image represents flowing and combed color behavior.

supports: colors floated on a bath and transferred

patterns.term_scope: material-inspired pattern family derived from terrazzo composite chips rather than one fixed printed motif
patterns.structure: Irregular chips of varied sizes, shapes and colors are scattered densely in a contrasting matrix, creating a non-directional granular field.

color_guidance.reason: Multisize chips on a contrasting ground are the key cue; actual terrazzo materials use many aggregate palettes.

patterns.qualification: Terrazzo is a composite material; “terrazzo pattern” is a material-inspired visual family based on scattered aggregate chips, not one fixed repeat.

supports: terrazzo as composite of marble/quartz/granite/glass chips with binder
